name: Treaty with the Ottawa, 1833 (Maumee)
aka: Treaty with the Ottawa band on the Miami of Lake Erie, February 18, 1833
nations: Ottawa Tribe of Oklahoma (treaty-era Maumee Band of Ottawa)
promises: Article 2: named reserves to be patented to named individuals out of the ceded land, those of the Indian grantees not to be sold without the President's approval.
Article 3: the United States would pay the band $29,440, applied at the band's direction to its debts.
Article 3: a band claim of $18,000 said to be owed under the 1831 Gardiner treaty was noted, with payments to named creditors to come out of it when paid.

breaches.what: The Indian Claims Commission found the 26,981.74 acres ceded by this treaty had a fair market value of $230,000 on March 22, 1833, held that the $29,440 paid was so grossly inadequate as to be unconscionable, and awarded $200,560 less offsets.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Indian Claims Commission, Ottawa Tribe et al. v. United States, Docket 304, 25 Ind. Cl. Comm. 1 (1971)

source.title: Ottawa Tribe et al. v. United States, Docket 304, Opinion of the Commission (March 17, 1971)
source.publisher: Oklahoma State University Library, Indian Claims Commission Decisions

breaches.quote: so grossly inadequate as to be unconscionable within the meaning of section 2, clause 3, of the Indian Claims Commission Act

landTaken: The Commission found Royce Area 183 contained 6,743.82 acres after individual grants and Royce Area 182 contained 20,237.92 acres as ceded, a net cession of 26,981.74 acres.
compensation: Final award of April 25, 1973: $182,610.00 in full satisfaction of the claims in Docket 304, after the parties stipulated that $17,950.00 had been paid.
today: The final award was entered in 1973. How the judgment funds were used was not traced.

nationVoice.summary: The Tribe describes itself as a sovereign Anishinaabe nation with deep roots in the Great Lakes region and the Ohio Valley, which entered into numerous treaties with the United States, most recently in 1862 and 1867.

openQuestions: Audit 2026-11-08: the Final Award (30 Ind. Cl. Comm. 206) was reopened; '$182,610.00 in full satisfaction of all claims presented in Docket 304' is legible, and it follows the parties' stipulation that $17,950.00 claimed as offsets had been paid. Figures, acreages and the quote match the 1971 opinion and findings.
Whether the $18,000 the band said was owed under the 1831 treaty was ever paid was not traced (Docket 305 concerns the 1831 treaty).

plain.promised: In return for its two reserves on the Maumee River in Ohio, the Ottawa band would get $29,440, paid toward its debts, and some named people would keep small reserves.
plain.happened: The Indian Claims Commission found in 1971 that the land was worth $230,000 and that paying $29,440 was unconscionable.
plain.today: The Commission entered a final award of $182,610.00 in 1973.
